candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents both pericarditis features (PR-segment depression, diffuse ST elevations, elevated inflammatory markers, viral prodrome) AND myocardial injury (troponin I 6.18 ng/mL, markedly elevated), with normal coronary arteries excluding ischemic MI. The reference diagnosis of myopericarditis requires both components. 'Acute pericarditis' captures only the pericardial component and does not account for the significant troponin elevation indicating myocardial involvement.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute pericarditis is the pericardial component of myopericarditis but omits the myocardial injury component required by the reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Troponin I 6.18 ng/mL is substantially elevated, strongly supporting myocardial involvement beyond isolated pericarditis
Normal coronary angiography excludes obstructive CAD as cause of troponin rise, consistent with myopericarditis
